where \VAR{internalF} is a freshly generated name.
Functional method declarations may be overloaded with top-level function
declarations.
An abstract function declaration
(described in \secref{abstractFunctionDeclarations})
can be provided also for overloaded functional method declarations.
See \chapref{multiple-dispatch} for a discussion of overloaded
functionals in Fortress.



When a method declaration includes a body expression, it is called a
\emph{method definition}.
A method declaration that does not have its body expression is referred to
as an \emph{abstract method declaration}.
An abstract method declaration declares an \emph{abstract method};
any object inheriting an abstract method must define a body expression for the
method.  An abstract method declaration may include the modifier \KWD{abstract}.
It may elide parameter names but parameter
types cannot be omitted except for the self parameter.


\note{
Method declarations that are overridden by some declaration are not
accessible.  They are not considered for overloading checks.

Partial overriding of an overloaded functional is allowed
but partial overriding of a functional declaration is not allowed.
}

A method declaration may have the modifier \KWD{override}.
Such a declaration \emph{overrides} any inherited declaration with the same name
and the self parameter (if any) at the same position,
whose parameter type, not counting the type of the self parameter,
is a strict subtype of the overriding declaration's parameter type.
The return type of the overriding declaration must be subtype of
that of the overridden declaration to preserve type safety.
A declaration with the modifier \KWD{override} must override
some inherited declaration.
It is a static error if a declaration with the modifier \KWD{override}
does not override any inherited declaration.

Here is an example trait \TYP{Enzyme} which provides methods
\VAR{reactionSpeed} and \VAR{catalyze}:
\input{\home/basic/examples/Trait.Method.e.tex}
\TYP{Enzyme}
inherits the abstract method \VAR{mass} from \TYP{OrganicMolecule},
declares the abstract method \VAR{reactionSpeed}, and
declares the concrete method \VAR{catalyze}
which is inherited as an abstract method
from its supertrait \TYP{Catalyst}.

     2	export Executable
     3	
     4	(* A sum or a product with a generator clause list and no static argument, whose element type nothing at the call fixes, runs on its elements under walk, an empty one too. *)
     5	
     6	emptySum(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = SUM[j <- 0#n] j
     7	
     8	run() = do
     9	    println("REACHED")
    10	    e = emptySum(0)
    11	    assert(e, 0, "reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\"; defining-generators.tex, subsection \"Simple Desugaring of Expressions with Generators\"")
    12	    s = SUM[j <- 0#4] j
    13	    assert(s, 6, "reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\"; defining-generators.tex, subsection \"Simple Desugaring of Expressions with Generators\"")
    14	    p = PROD[j <- 1#3] j
    15	    assert(p, 6, "reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\"; defining-generators.tex, subsection \"Simple Desugaring of Expressions with Generators\"")
    16	    println("PASS")
    17	  end
    18	
    19	end
=== InferUnfixedFBoundedWalk.fss
     1	component InferUnfixedFBoundedWalk
     2	import Set.{...}
     3	export Executable
     4	
     5	(* A type parameter whose bound mentions itself and that nothing at a call fixes is left open under walk: every value is admitted where its type is expected, so a reduction with no static argument runs on its elements' own types. *)
     6	
     7	trait Cmp[\T\] end
     8	
     9	object BoxU[\T\]()
    10	    getter kind(): String = "boxed"
    11	end
    12	
    13	mk[\T extends Cmp[\T\]\](): BoxU[\T\] = BoxU[\T\]()
    14	
    15	run(): () = do
    16	    r = SUM[j <- 0#4] (j / 2.0)
    17	    assert(r, 3.0, "a sum of RR64 elements with no static argument joins its elements with their own + (reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\")")
    18	    p = PROD[j <- 1#0] j
    19	    assert(p, 1, "an empty product of ZZ32 elements with no static argument is the identity 1 (reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\")")
    20	    lo = BIG MIN[j <- 0#4] (j - 2)
    21	    assert(lo, -2, "BIG MIN with no static argument over j - 2 for j in 0#4 is -2 (reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\")")
    22	    hi = BIG MAX[j <- 0#4] (j - 2)
    23	    assert(hi, 1, "BIG MAX with no static argument over j - 2 for j in 0#4 is 1 (reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\")")
    24	    s = { n^2 | n <- -2:2 }
    25	    assert(|s|, 3, "a set comprehension with no static argument over n^2 for n in -2:2 holds three elements (comprehensions.tex, section \"Comprehensions\")")
    26	    assert((0 IN s) AND (1 IN s) AND (4 IN s), true, "the set comprehension over n^2 for n in -2:2 holds 0, 1 and 4 (comprehensions.tex, section \"Comprehensions\")")
    27	    b = mk()
    28	    assert(b.kind, "boxed", "a call that fixes no static argument of a function whose type parameter's bound mentions itself runs, and its result answers its getter (inference.tex, section \"The Static Arguments of a Call\")")
    29	    assert("ab.c".upto('.'), "ab", "String's upto, whose body calls BIG MIN with no static argument, answers the prefix before the character")
    30	    println("PASS")
    31	  end
    32	
    33	end

     1	component OverrideInTraitWalk
     2	export Executable

     4	(* A trait whose method declaration with the modifier override overrides an inherited one does not inherit it, so an object below that trait runs the overriding declaration, under walk. *)

     8	  dot(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = 1
     9	end
    10	trait W extends S

    12	  override dot(x: Number): ZZ32 = 2
    13	end
    14	object Wo extends W end
    15

    18	    assert(Wo.dot(3), 2, "W's dotted method dot over Number overrides S's over ZZ32, so Wo.dot(3) runs W's (traits.tex, section \"Method Declarations\")")
    19	    println("PASS")
    20	  end
    21	
    22	end

| 20 | an aggregate's element type is computed from the elements' **runtime class**, and `List` is invariant, so `<\|1.0,1.0\|>` is `List[\FloatLiteral\]` and explicit `[\T\]` ascriptions are mandatory in data/plumbing code | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (walk) | `basic/expressions/aggregate.tex`, "List Expressions" (the element type is the union of the element types) | none | ours, blinded | siblings: 96, 432. `explorations/spec-probes/p1_infer.fss` infers when the runtime class *is* the target. The same defect shows as `ArrayList[\__DefaultVector[…]\] is not assignable to List[\Vector[…]\]` (`explorations/matrix-ad-probes/REPORT.md` Q1). A declared type drives the literal: a heterogeneous `<\| a, c, o \|>` of three object types is accepted where `List[\Node\]` is declared on the left (`explorations/run-b/probes/c11_object_model.fss`), so the defect is the missing join, not the ascription. On the flat tower the run-time element type fails the F-bounds of `SUM`, `PROD` and `BIG MAX` (row 432). probe and full text: history, row 20 |
| 364 | **walk infers a generic object's static argument from the argument's run-time class**: for `object Cell[\T extends Any\](v: T) end`, `Cell("s")` prints `Cell[\FlatString\]` and `Cell(3)` `Cell[\Int\]`, where the compiled path prints `Cell[\String\]` and `Cell[\IntLiteral\]` | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (walk) | `basic/expressions/literals.tex`, "Literals" (a string literal has type `String`); `basic/inference.tex`, "The Static Arguments of a Call" | `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXInferredStaticArgRungS.fss` | climb batch 3 rung S | The site, the inference of a static argument at a constructor call, which reads the value's run-time class, is not located; rung K's inference keeps it for arguments of one class. Only the string case is asserted: a numeral's type is `NaturalNumeral[\n,10,v\]`, which neither path implements. The run-time class also makes walk refuse well-typed bindings, `a: BoxT[\ZZ32\] = BoxT(z)` for `z: ZZ32`, "RHS expression type BoxT[\Int\] is not assignable" (`XXXInferredIntBindingRungT`), and a `Box[\Int\]` dispatches past `Box[\ZZ32\]` and `Box[\Number\]` to `Any`. Workaround: write it, `Cell[\String\]("s")`. full text: history, row 364 |
| 628 | the reductions' `Any` and `AnyMaybe` devices, which the compiled checker refuses, keep walk's reductions running where walk erases an unwritten static argument to `Bottom` | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | design limit (library) | `Specification/basic/expressions/if.tex`, "If Expressions"; `Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex`, "Summations and Other Reduction Expressions" | `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv` | climb batch 10 rung G | At `9c9e823d5`: `AssociativeReduction`'s `simpleJoin(a:Any, b:Any): Any`, which its eight implementers declare at the element type (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3271` to `:3478`); the lifted type `AnyMaybe`, no `Condition`, so `if av <- a` cannot bind (`:3089` to `:3126`); `MonoidReduction`'s `lift(r:Any): R` (`:3144`) against the api's `lift(r:R)`. With `simpleJoin` at `R`, `BIG MIN <\|[\ZZ32\] 4, 2, 7 \|>` stops ('... has neither body nor def'); with `MinReduction`'s at `T` too, `BIG MIN[i <- 0#4] (3 - i)` is refused ('simpleJoin param 1 (a:BOTTOM) got arg 1: ZZ32'); the base prints `2` and `0`. Fix after row 424: both at `R`, lifted type `Maybe[\R\]`. full text: history, row 628 |
| 425 | **the compiled checker instantiates a generic big operator's static parameter in an unwritten clause form at its bound, never from the clauses or the expected type**: with the bound `Number`, `s: ZZ32 = BIG LAST[j <- lo#n] (3 j)` is refused, and an F-bounded one (`BIG MIN`) has no instance | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (checker) | `Specification/advanced/parallelism-locality/defining-generators.tex`, "Simple Desugaring of Expressions with Generators" | `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/InferBigOperatorUnwritten.fss` | ours (sum-replacement judgement) | siblings: 424. The test's `BIG LAST` with the bound `Number` is refused, 'Right-hand side has type Number, but declared type is ZZ32' (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/REPORT.md` section 4): the desugaring makes the big operator an argument of `__bigOperator`, typed before that call with no expected type. `BIG MIN` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4137` at 493b4076f) reads 'not applicable to an argument of type ()'. Inferring from the clauses means one inference across a lambda's body, which the checker avoids (`hasInferenceVars`). Workaround: write the static argument. full text: history, row 425 |
| 555 | under walk, a call to a generic function whose lone type parameter is fixed by arguments whose types share two or more unrelated minimal supertypes fails when the parameter's bound mentions itself, as `T extends Cmp[\T\]` does | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (walk) | `basic/inference.tex`, "The Static Arguments of a Call" | none | climb batch 7b rung L | siblings: 589, 591. Fixed half (669b77d03, climb batch 9, rung W; `ProjectFortress/tests/InferTwoCommonParentsWalk.fss`): where walk instantiates a call's declaration, a join of several minimal common supertypes takes the parameter's bound. Open half: with `trait Red extends Cmp[\Red\]`, `trait Round extends Cmp[\Round\]`, `fF[\T extends Cmp[\T\]\](a: T, b: T)` called `fF(Apple, Cherry)` prints 'Cannot unify Any(...FTypeTop) with Cmp[\T\](...TraitType) abm=T=(Any,Any)' (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-instance/REPORT.md` section 12, `RpFJoin`). == explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record

POSITIONS.md:123
- **The order of the work after batch 10.** First the skills. `fortress-repo` is rewritten whole by the outline and the seven principles, every part cold-read and fixed. He read and approved `SKILL.md`'s "How a program runs" and the three testing parts; the rest is not held for his reading before batch 11. The three approved parts go through the same pass, and a Fable reviewer compares them with the versions he approved, writing a synthesis of the two where it finds a regression, never a wholesale revert. `coordinator` and `cloud-container` follow later. Then the batch workflow is redesigned: an Opus synthesis of the six batch-10 designs and the measurements of where the batches' tokens went, built into the script with batch 11's manifest, and reviewed by Fable instead of by him. Then batch 11 runs, launched overnight on the standing go, its questions Q1 to Q4 at their recommendations, resumed after the weekly reset if the limit stops it; it is to show the better shape against the wasteful runs before it. The reason for the order: the recent climbing was token-inefficient because the batches re-ran their costly parts, and those causes are what started the skill extraction; a batch run before both are done repeats them.
